 Judgment

The present claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of MV Act 1989 by the minor injured petitioner through her natural guardian, seeking compensation of .13,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. Petitioner has stated that on 28.02.2023 at about 3-50 p.m. petitioner got down from the school bus and was crossing the road to go to her house,at Vijayanagar main road, white filed, Bengaluru city.
At that time, rider of a motor cycle bearing reg no.KA-53- HM-6213 riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner on Nagagondanahalli, Vijayanagar main road and collided with the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

She was Immediately shifted to Manipal Hospital, Varthur road, Bengaluru, where she recieved treatment as an inpatient, and incurred medical expenses amounting to .2,50,000/-, nourishment and food amounting to .75,000/, and conveying amounting Rs 40,000/- The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle.
3. At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 7 years and was a student.
Due to the injuries sustained, she was unable to attend the school or participate in curricular and extra curricular activities, which has adversely affected her education and future prospects.

4. The Petitioner claims that the Respondents, being the owner and insurer of the alleged offending vehicle, jointly and severally liable to pay compensation along with interest for injuries, pain suffering and financial loss caused by the accident.
5. In response to the petition, Respondent No. 1 has appeared before this Court through counsel and filed a written statement.

Respondent No. 2 has not appeared despite service of notice and was accordingly placed ex parte.
6.
In the written statement, the respondent no 2 admitted issuing of a liability only insurance policy but stated that their liability is subject to terms and conditions of the said policy.
They have further contended that the owner of the offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) of MV Act.

Respondent no 2 denied the negligence of the rider of offending vehicle and further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL and as such, this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.

It is also denied the nature of injuries, the Chilakuri Medha vs Ganga Ram Jaishi on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199413473/
2 occupation and income of the Petitioner, the disability and the amount claimed as compensation,
terming it as excessive and exaggerated.

sentences.text: On these grounds, they have prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the basis of the above, the following Issues arise for my consideration :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in an accident when she was crossing the road infront of Mangolia Apt road, 1st Cross, Nagondanahalli,
Vijayanagar main road, white filed, Bengaluru District on 28.02.2023 at about 3.50 p.m only due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-HM-6213 ?

2. What compensation petitioner is entitled?
3. What order?
8. In order to prove the claim, the natural guardian/father of Petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P-17.

On the other hand the Respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.R1 to 3.
9.

I have heard the counsel for Petitioner and perused the material on record.
10.

By considering the evidences, arguments and the other materials available on record, I have answered the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1:- Since the Petitioner being minor, represented by her natural guardian/father.
Natural guardian has examined as PW-1.

petitioner got down from the school bus and was crossing the road to go to her house,at Vijayanagar main road, white filed, Bengaluru city.

and collided with the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

She was Immediately shifted to Manipal Hospital, Varthur road,
Bengaluru, where she recieved treatment as an inpatient 12.
PW.1 had given the first information statement to the Police as per Ex.P.2 on the basis of which Ex.P.1 FIR was registered.
Spot Mahazar, rough sketch and vehicle seizure mahazar were drawn by the Police as per Ex.P.3 and 4.
The notice under Section 133 MV Act is marked at Ex.P5.
Reply to notice is marked at Ex.P6.
The offending vehicle was inspected as per IMV report at Ex.P.7 and after completion of investigation, charge sheet is filed by the concerned Police at Ex.P.9.

sentences.text:
As per Ex.P.8 and 14 wound certificate and discharge summary, the Petitioner has sustained injuries as below;
(1) Multiple contusions present over the face with right frontal region hematoma.
(2) Multiple small lacerated wound present over head, chin, lip and right hand fingers.
(3) Head injury.
(a) Subdural hematoma along left tentorium.
(b) Fracture of right frontal bone extending to orbital roof with displaced fracture fragments in to right orbit.
(c) Acute cerebral order.
(d) Intracranial hemorrhage.
(4) Right eye ecchymosis subconjunctival hemorrhage.
It is mentioned that the injuries no.1,2,4 are simple in nature and injuries no. 3 (a,b,c,d) are grievous in nature.
Further as per Ex.P.14 - discharge summary, she has sustained fracture of right frontal bone extending to orbital roof with displaced fracture fragments into right orbit.

14. The Respondent-Insurance Company has contended that the accident did not occur due to the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle, but rather due to the negligence of the petitioner or PW1.
In support of this contention, certain suggestions were put forth during the cross-examination of the petitioner.
15. It was suggested to the PW1 that the accident was caused due to his own negligence.
He denied the suggestion that if he had been more cautious while crossing on the road, the accident could have been avoided.

However, apart from these suggestions made during cross-examination and the general denials in the written statement, the Respondent has not produced any corroborative evidence to establish that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner or from her parent.
16. There is no material on record to disprove the evidence adduced by the petitioner or to substantiate the contentions raised by the respondent no 2.
The testimony of PW1 is duly corroborated by the documentary evidence produced on record.
Nothing substantial has been elicited during cross-examination to discredit or shake the credibility of the petitioner's case.

17. It is a well-settled principle of law that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation,
and the Claims Tribunal is not required to insist on strict proof of rashness and negligence as demanded in criminal trials.

In the present case, after due investigation, the police have filed a Chilakuri Medha vs Ganga Ram Jaishi on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199413473/
4 charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle, which is marked as Exhibit P9.

entities.text: Chilakuri Medha vs Ganga Ram Jaishi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This, along with other documentary evidence on record, prima facie establishes the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

Hence, based on the totality of the evidence, both oral and documentary, it is clearly established that the petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident caused solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle's rider.

Hence,
Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

18. ISSUE NO.2 :-The Petitioner was 7 years old at the time of accident and has sustained a fracture of right frontal bone extending to orbital roof with displaced fracture in to right orbit, scalp hematoma in right front region and injuries to other parts of the body and taken to Manipal Hospital, Varthur road, Bengaluru city and private clinics, where she has received treatment as an inpatient.
Due to the accidental injuries she was not able to attend her classes for considerable period.
19. There is no materials on record to establish that the Petitioner has suffered any loss to her educational career as a result of the accident.
Accordingly no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of education due to the accidental injuries.
20. The PW1 has stated that she has incurred Rs.3,40,000/- towards medical and incidental expenses during the period of hospitalization.
In this regard, he has produced the medical bills at Ex.P.17 amounting to Rs.1,10,443/-.
It appears that PW1 has incurred Rs 1,10,443/- towards medical expenses.
21. On perusal of EX P16 it appears that the petitioner has taken conservative.
There is no doubt that the petitioner sustained a injuries to her head .
However, PW1 has not examined the doctor to establish that she has suffered any permanent disability.

Nevertheless, considering the grievous nature of the injury and in the absence of medical evidence specifically quantifying disability, this tribunal is of view that the petitioner must have endured considerable pain and suffering.
Taking into account her young age and the physical and emotional distress caused by the injury, this court deems it appropriate to award global compensation.
under all the conventional heads.
22. Liability:

Respondent No. 2-Insurance Company has specifically contended that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, inasmuch as the rider was not holding a valid and effective Driving License (DL) as on the date of the accident.

On this ground, the Insurance Company claims that it is not liable to indemnify the owner and is, therefore,
absolved of any liability to pay compensation to the petitioner.

23. To support his case the Respondent no 2 has relied upon the decisions rendered in SLP 11757/2025 between Mahaveer V United India Insurance Co Ltd.
24.

entities.text: Mahaveer V United India Insurance Co Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To substantiate this contention, Respondent No. 2 examined its official as RW1, who deposed that the rider of the offending vehicle was not duly licensed and thus the insurance company is not liable due to breach of fundamental policy conditions.

RW1 relied upon the notice issued to the Chilakuri Medha vs Ganga Ram Jaishi on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199413473/
5 owner (Ex- R-2), and the reply received (Ex -R-3) from Respondent No.1, who is the owner-cum-driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Chilakuri Medha vs Ganga Ram Jaishi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this reply, the owner failed to produce a valid DL,
thereby supporting the insurance company's assertion.

25. Furthermore, Ex P-9 -Charge Sheet reveals that the driver was charge-sheeted under Section 279 and 338 IPC, read with Sections 181,180 and 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act, indicating that he did not hold a valid or effective DL at the time of the accident, further strengthening the contention of the insurance company.

26. It is also pertinent to note that Respondent No. 1, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, has neither contested the proceedings nor produced any rebuttal evidence either oral or documentary to establish that he held a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.

27. In view of the unrebutted evidence on record, this Tribunal holds that the rider of the offending vehicle, namely Bharat Jaishi, was not holding a valid and effective Driving License at the relevant time.
This clearly constitutes a willful breach of the terms and conditions of the policy contract.
28.In view of above discussion, the Respondent No.2 (Insurance Company) is not liable to indemnify the insured for the claim made under the present petition.

Consequently, Respondent No.
1, being the owner of the offending vehicle, is held liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

29. The learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that, notwithstanding the violation of policy terms, the Tribunal ought to have directed the insurance company to pay the compensation initially and thereafter recover the same from the insured, invoking the principle of "pay and recovery".
In support of this contention, reliance was placed on certain decisions rendered between MFA 202104/2024 between The branch Managerr ICICI Lombard Nibhaye Vadde V Pooja and others.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard Nibhaye Vadde V Pooja
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 30. However, upon careful perusal material on record and legal position, it is pertinent to note that the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, particularly relevant provisions that impact liability of insurers, came into effect from 15-02-2022.
Since this amendment relates to substantive rights, it has only prospective effect, and cannot be applied retrospectively to the present case.

Hence, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the principle of pay and recover does not arise, and the liability to pay compensation rests solely with Respondent No.1, the owner of the offending vehicle.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
31. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of . 2,00,000/- together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of petition till the realization.
